Hi, Giovanna. Nice to finally talk. I listened to your message twice.
Hi, Ryan. Nice to meet you. Sorry, my English is slow today.
Slow is fine. Slow is better than nothing. So, what do you study?
I study Administration at university, and I also do a Fashion course at night.
Two courses at the same time? How is your schedule?
It is full. Classes every morning, and the Fashion course twice a week.
And you travel a lot, right? Your message said the United States.
Yes, but always with my family. Next time I want to go alone.

Sorry, could you say that again, more slowly?

Hi, my name is Ryan. I am nineteen years old and I am from Denver, in Colorado. I study Business at a state university, and this is my second year. My week is busy. I have classes in the morning, and three afternoons a week I work in a coffee shop near the campus. I do not have much free time, but I like it that way. I am learning Portuguese because my grandmother is Brazilian, and I want to visit Sao Paulo next year. My Portuguese is not good yet. I understand a lot when people speak slowly, but when I try to answer, I stop in the middle of the sentence. So I know exactly how you feel. If you speak slowly for me, I will speak slowly for you. That is the deal.

The first time I travelled without my family, I was eighteen. My mother came with me to the airport, and she stayed with me until the gate. After that I was alone for eleven hours. I remember two things from that flight. The first one is that nothing terrible happened. I found my seat, I ate the food, I slept a little, and the plane landed. The second one is more useful. Every time somebody spoke to me in English, I understood the question, and then I answered with one word. Yes. No. Coffee. Thank you. One word is not a conversation. Nobody laughs at your grammar on a plane, but a one word answer ends the conversation before it starts. Now I answer with a full sentence, even a short one, and people talk to me.
